title: The release that passed every check
summary: A new version shipped. Health checks are green. A quarter of requests are failing.

statement.situation: Your service handles 3,000 requests/s. A new release goes out at 1 minute in. Its health checks pass, but it quietly returns errors on a quarter of the requests it serves. Nobody notices until customers complain — unless your deployment process notices first.
symptoms: Errors rise gradually as the rollout proceeds
By the time someone investigates, the whole fleet runs the bad version
requirements: Limit how many users ever see the bad version
Detect and undo the release automatically
Don't lose capacity (or money) just to deploy safely
constraints: Budget: $3.00/hour at peak (including extra capacity during a rollout)
New instances take 30 s to start
You can't make the new version better — only control how it's released

learningObjectives: Blast radius and exposure over time
Why health checks don't catch correctness regressions
Rollback speed and capacity during a rollback

references.title: Kubernetes: liveness, readiness and startup probes

scenarios.name: Release with 25% errors at t=60 s
scenarios.description: 3,000 req/s for 8 minutes. At t=60 s a release is rolled out. The new version fails 25% of the requests it handles.

successCriteria.label: Total error volume stays small (≤ 1.5% of all requests)
Fully healthy again within 3 minutes of the release
Capacity never dips enough to cause its own errors
